symptom: my hand-rolled GPIO driver maps /dev/mem and pokes the BCM2835 GPIO registers directly. On the Pi 5 it reads back zeros and pins never toggle. It worked on the Pi 4.

files.mmio.py:
import mmap, os
# Map the BCM2835 GPIO registers via /dev/mem and set bit 17.
fd = os.open('/dev/mem', os.O_RDWR)
base = 0x3F200000
m = mmap.mmap(fd, 4096, offset=base)
m[0x1C] = 1 << 17   # GPSET0
os.close(fd)

gold.diagnosis: On the Pi 5 the GPIO controller is on the RP1 southbridge, not at the legacy BCM2835 0x3F200000 mmio base, so /dev/mem pokes silently miss. The correct abstraction is the Linux GPIO character device (/dev/gpiochip4) via libgpiod (the gpiod Python bindings). Rewrite to drive the line through a libgpiod LineRequest.
